caption: Graphic shows an enlarged and inflamed epididymis enveloping the testis posteriorly. Note that the testis appears normal in size and configuration.
Graphic shows an irregularly enlarged epididymis with focal cystic areas , indicating early liquefaction and necrosis.

Color Doppler US of the bilateral epididymal tail in a 24-year-old man with acute right testicular pain reveals enlargement and marked hyperemia of the right epididymal tail, consistent with acute epididymitis.

Color Doppler US of the bilateral epididymis in a 20-year-old man with acute right scrotal pain reveals enlargement and marked hyperemia of the right epididymal head compared to the left , consistent with acute epididymitis.

Sagittal grayscale US of the right testis and epididymis in a 23-year-old man with acute scrotal pain shows an enlarged epididymal tail with diffuse heterogeneity and "mass-like" appearance , which is a typical appearance for acute epididymitis.
Side-by-side color Doppler US of the testicles bilaterally shows the left testicle is markedly hyperemic in comparison to the right, consistent with left-sided orchitis.

Color Doppler US reveals a round, focal, hypoechoic region within the right testicle with increased vascularity . Normal testicular parenchyma can be seen adjacent to this area . This was a case of focal orchitis.

Color Doppler US of bilateral testes demonstrates heterogenous echogenicity and decreased vascularity within the left testicle , consistent with testicular infarction. This was the sequela of venous thrombosis secondary to orchitis.

Color Doppler US of the left epididymis reveals a markedly hyperemic tail with a heterogenous hypoechoic lesion centrally . The findings are consistent with epididymitis complicated by an epididymal abscess.

Color Doppler US of the right testis in a patient who presented with acute epididymoorchitis reveals a hypoechoic, thick-walled lesion within the testicle with peripheral hyperemia, consistent with a testicular abscess.
Graphic shows epididymitis with an inflamed, hyperemic epididymal body draped over a normal-appearing testicle. In epididymoorchitis, the testicle would also be inflamed.
Longitudinal oblique color Doppler US shows marked hyperemia of the left testis and epididymis in a teenager with acute pain, consistent with epididymoorchitis.

Transverse grayscale US in a 5-year-old boy with acute right scrotal swelling shows asymmetric enlargement and heterogeneous echotexture of the epididymis . The testicle has normal echotexture but was larger than the contralateral side. A small, simple hydrocele is also present.
Color Doppler US in the same patient shows marked hyperemia of the right epididymis, testicle, and surrounding scrotal tissues, consistent with epididymoorchitis.

Anterior 5-minute image from a Tc-99m pertechnetate scan in a 17-year-old with left scrotal pain demonstrates ↑ radiotracer uptake at the left testicle compared to the right , which can be seen with epididymoorchitis.

Coronal T2 FS MR in a 12-year-old with 1 week of right hip pain shows marked high signal intensity throughout the right hemiscrotum , suspicious for epididymoorchitis or subacute torsion given the duration of his symptoms.
Transverse side-by-side US performed following the MR shows an enlarged right testicle , enlarged heterogeneous epididymis , hydrocele , and right-sided scrotal wall thickening.

Transverse side-by-side color Doppler US in the same patient shows hyperemia in all of the right-sided scrotal structures compared to the left, confirming right epididymoorchitis. There was no evidence of testicular torsion.
Transverse US in a 6-year-old boy who had marked scrotal swelling on the left shows a hydrocele , enlarged heterogeneous epididymis , and scrotal wall thickening .
Transverse side-by-side color Doppler US in the same patient shows marked hyperemia of all the left-sided scrotal contents, consistent with epididymoorchitis.

Longitudinal color Doppler US of the inguinal canal in a 2-year-old boy shows hyperemia of the spermatic cord , epididymis , and testis , along with hydrocele fluid, consistent with epididymoorchitis.

Transverse side-by-side color Doppler US of the testes is very useful to assess overall size/symmetry of testes, blood flow, and echotexture. Although the left testis is not dramatically hyperemic , it is larger than the right and has a surrounding hydrocele , suggesting orchitis.
Sagittal color Doppler US shows dramatic hyperemia throughout an enlarged epididymis in a patient with epididymitis but no orchitis.
Transverse US in a young patient shows right-sided scrotal wall thickening , a hydrocele, and an enlarged heterogeneous epididymis . The right testicle is also larger than the left.

Transverse power Doppler US in the same patient shows hyperemia in the right testicle and epididymis , confirming epididymoorchitis. The side-by-side transverse view is helpful to compare blood flow in the scrotal structures.

Transverse US shows a whorled appearance of thickened, heterogeneous epididymis in a teenager with several days of pain, suggesting epididymitis. In such cases, it is critical to confirm that the whorled heterogeneous structures do not represent a twisted spermatic cord. Confirmation of increased low-resistance flow is also helpful to confirm epididymoorchitis.

Longitudinal oblique US of the epididymal head in a teenager with focal pain on the left side shows a small hydrocele and an enlarged left epididymal head . The findings are suspicious for epididymitis.
Sagittal color Doppler US shows abundant color signal in this mildly enlarged testicle and epididymis . There is also a small hydrocele on the symptomatic side in this patient with epididymoorchitis.
Sagittal color Doppler US of the same patient's contralateral testis shows normal blood flow on the boy's asymptomatic side.
Transverse US shows a very echogenic testicle medially and an enlarged hypoechoic epididymis with hydrocele laterally. Note the posterior shadowing from the testicular microlithiasis.
Transverse color Doppler US in the same patient shows hyperemia involving only the epididymis with normal flow in the testicle, consistent with isolated epididymitis.

Sagittal US shows a swirled, heterogeneous echotexture in a dramatically enlarged epididymis with a surrounding anechoic hydrocele in a case of isolated epididymitis without associated orchitis. It is critical in such patients to confirm that the structures above the testicle do not represent a twisted spermatic cord.

Sagittal US shows a heterogeneous, mostly echogenic, enlarged epididymis , enlarged testicle , and small anechoic reactive hydrocele in this boy with epididymoorchitis (as confirmed by hyperemic flow to the epididymis and testicle on color Doppler imaging, not shown). It is critical in such patients to confirm that the structures above the testicle do not represent a twisted spermatic cord. Demonstrating ↑ low-resistance arterial flow in the testicle can help confirm an inflammatory cause for this appearance.

Grayscale US in a 5-year-old boy with acute left scrotal swelling shows marked enlargement and heterogeneous echotexture of the epididymis . The testicle has a normal echotexture but was larger than the contralateral side.

Longitudinal color Doppler US of the same 5-year-old boy with left scrotal swelling shows enlargement of the epididymis and testis with ↑ blood flow and a surrounding hydrocele, consistent with epididymoorchitis.
Longitudinal oblique color Doppler US shows a thickened, hyperemic, and heterogeneous epididymis in a teenager with several days of pain, consistent with epididymitis.
